overview.description: Electronic lab notebooks (Benchling) and LIMS are the backbone of an industry lab: versioned plasmid maps, sample tracking, inventory, and results tied to metadata. FAIR, well-annotated data is what makes a result reproducible and a candidate employable.
objectives: keep a versioned, searchable electronic record (Benchling ELN)
track samples, plates, and inventory through a LIMS
annotate data with metadata so it is Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, Reusable (FAIR)
manage plasmid maps and sequences digitally, not in scattered files

steps.description: Electronic lab notebooks (Benchling) and LIMS are the backbone of an industry lab: versioned plasmid maps, sample tracking, inventory, and results tied to metadata. FAIR, well-annotated data is what makes a result reproducible and a candidate employable.
steps.intro: The difference between an academic and an industry lab is often the data discipline: nothing is real until it is recorded, versioned, and findable by someone else.

instructions.title: Structure the record
instructions.description: Set up an ELN with a consistent experiment template: objective, method, materials (linked), results, conclusion.

instructions.title: Track physical samples
instructions.description: Register plasmids, strains, and plates with unique IDs and locations so any tube is traceable.

instructions.title: Annotate for FAIR
instructions.description: Attach metadata (conditions, batch, operator, instrument) so data can be reused and audited later.

instructions.title: Version everything
instructions.description: Keep sequence/plasmid edits versioned; never overwrite - the history is part of the record.

submission.description: Set up a small ELN/LIMS record for one experiment with linked materials, sample IDs, and FAIR metadata; explain how someone else could reproduce it from your record alone.
